```{r}
#install necessary packages

install.packages("nflverse")
library("nflverse")
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(naniar)
library(ggplot2)
```

#this block is just code to copy so we have the same type of process when combining data & look at my creating columns block in case you want to use those columns aswell  

```{r}

#this is how u grab your division & change to fit your division
my_division <- c("BAL", "CLE", "CIN", "PIT")

#put the code below in your block & modify it to work for your division
clean_schedule <- load_schedules(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(
    location == "Home",
    game_type == "REG", #excludes neutral sites
    home_team %in% my_division | away_team %in% my_division
  ) %>%
  select(game_id, season, home_team, away_team, home_score, away_score, result, location, roof)


#this function will take a while to load 
my_pbp <-load_pbp(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(
    game_id %in% clean_schedule$game_id, #matches the function so we can join them
    !is.na(play_type)
  )%>%
  select(game_id, posteam_type, epa, penalty, penalty_type, penalty_team, 
    penalty_yards, pass_attempt, rush_attempt, yards_gained, 
    play_type, down, ydstogo, qtr, score_differential) 
#i added more variables to give more options incase you want to check dif variable correlation

division_df<- clean_pbp %>% left_join(clean_schedule, by="game_id")

```


Reuel's block
```{r}

reuel_division <- c("BAL", "CLE", "CIN", "PIT")

clean_schedule <- load_schedules(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(
    location == "Home",
    game_type == "REG", #excludes neutral sites
    home_team %in% reuel_division | away_team %in% reuel_division
  ) %>%
  select(game_id, season, home_team, away_team, home_score, away_score, result, location, roof)

my_pbp <-load_pbp(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(
    game_id %in% clean_schedule$game_id, #matches the function so we can join them
    !is.na(play_type)
  )%>%
  select(game_id, posteam_type, epa, penalty, penalty_type, penalty_team, 
    penalty_yards, pass_attempt, rush_attempt, yards_gained, 
    play_type, down, ydstogo, qtr, score_differential) 

division_df<- my_pbp %>% left_join(clean_schedule, by="game_id")
head(division_df)

#handling missing data
gg_miss_var(division_df)
division_df$penalty_yards <- replace_na(division_df$penalty_yards, 0)
```

#Creating new columns
```{r}
division_df <- division_df %>% 
  mutate(
    penalized_side = case_when(
      penalty_team == home_team ~ "Home",
      penalty_team == away_team ~ "Away",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_ #keeps na values as NA values
    )
  )

division_df <- division_df %>%
  mutate(
    is_covid_year = case_when(
      season == 2020 ~ 1, #covid year
      TRUE ~ 0 #every other year
    )
  )

#the first penalty type affects the home team more than the ref
#the second penalty type affects the refs calls
division_df <- division_df %>%
  mutate(
    penalty_category = case_when(
      is.na(penalty_type) ~ NA_character_,
      str_detect(penalty_type, "False Start|Delay of Game|Illegal Formation|Illegal Shift") ~ "Procedural (Crowd Noise)",
      str_detect(penalty_type, "Holding|Pass Interference|Roughing|Unnecessary Roughness|Face Mask|Horse Collar|Unsportsmanlike") ~ "Discretionary (Ref Judgment)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

#check to see if data is sorted properly
table(division_df$is_covid_year, useNA = "ifany")
```

Emily's block
```{r}

install.packages(c("nflreadr", "tidyverse", "stringr"))
library(nflreadr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

emily_division <- c("DEN", "KC", "LV", "LAC") 

clean_schedule <- load_schedules(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(
    location == "Home", 
    game_type == "REG", 
    home_team %in% emily_division | away_team %in% emily_division
  ) %>%
  select(game_id, season, home_team, away_team, home_score, 
         away_score, result, location, roof)

my_pbp <- load_pbp(2018:2022) %>%
  filter(game_id %in% clean_schedule$game_id)

division_df <- my_pbp %>% 
  left_join(clean_schedule, by = "game_id", suffix = c("", ".sched")) %>%
  mutate(penalty_yards = replace_na(penalty_yards, 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    penalized_side = case_when(
      penalty_team == home_team ~ "Home",
      penalty_team == away_team ~ "Away",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_ 
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_covid_year = case_when(
      season == 2020 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_indoor = case_when(
      roof %in% c("dome", "closed") ~ 1,
      roof %in% c("outdoors", "open") ~ 0
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    penalty_category = case_when(
      is.na(penalty_type) ~ NA_character_,
      str_detect(penalty_type, "False Start|Delay of Game|Illegal Formation|Illegal Shift") ~ "Procedural",
      str_detect(penalty_type, "Holding|Pass Interference|Roughing|Unnecessary Roughness|Face Mask|Horse Collar|Unsportsmanlike") ~ "Discretionary",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

penalty_breakdown <- division_df %>%
  filter(penalty == 1) %>% 
  group_by(penalty_type, is_covid_year, penalized_side) %>%
  summarise(total_calls = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = penalized_side, 
    values_from = total_calls, 
    values_fill = 0 
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff_away_minus_home = Away - Home
  ) %>%
  arrange(is_covid_year, desc(diff_away_minus_home))

print(penalty_breakdown, n = 30)

# plots for presentation
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Get the Top 10 penalties that drive the bias (where Away team was penalized most)
top_penalties <- penalty_breakdown %>%
  filter(is_covid_year == 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(diff_away_minus_home)) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  pull(penalty_type)

# 2. Filter the data for just those top 10 and plot
plot_data_top <- penalty_breakdown %>%
  filter(penalty_type %in% top_penalties) %>%
  # Change is_covid_year to a label for the legend
  mutate(Season_Type = ifelse(is_covid_year == 1, "2020 (No Fans)", "Normal (With Fans)"))

# 3. Create the plot
ggplot(plot_data_top, aes(x = reorder(penalty_type, diff_away_minus_home), 
                          y = diff_away_minus_home, 
                          fill = Season_Type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() + # Flips the chart so penalty names are readable
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2020 (No Fans)" = "pink", "Normal (With Fans)" = "navy")) +
  labs(
    title = "Which Penalties Drive Away-Team Bias in the AFC West?",
    subtitle = "Difference in calls (Away Penalties minus Home Penalties)",
    x = "Penalty Type",
    y = "Bias Differential (Positive = More calls against Away team)",
    fill = "Game Environment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )
  
# 1. Summarize the data by category
category_bias <- division_df %>%
  filter(penalty == 1) %>%
  group_by(penalty_category, is_covid_year, penalized_side) %>%
  summarise(total_calls = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = penalized_side, values_from = total_calls, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(diff_away_minus_home = Away - Home) %>%
  # Calculate the average differential per category
  group_by(penalty_category, is_covid_year) %>%
  summarise(avg_diff = mean(diff_away_minus_home, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Remove NA categories and "Other"
  filter(!is.na(penalty_category), penalty_category != "Other") %>%
  mutate(Season_Type = ifelse(is_covid_year == 1, "2020 (No Fans)", "Normal (With Fans)"))

# 2. Create the plot
ggplot(category_bias, aes(x = penalty_category, y = avg_diff, fill = Season_Type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2020 (No Fans)" = "pink", "Normal (With Fans)" = "navy")) +
  labs(
    title = "Referee Bias by Penalty Category",
    subtitle = "Did the absence of fans in 2020 reduce the bias?",
    x = "Penalty Category",
    y = "Avg Differential (Away - Home)",
    fill = "Game Environment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )
```
